verification.note: Printed pp. 42–43 read, including the explicit substantive discussion of Bederman’s argument and Harvey’s extension/qualification in her own object. Other pages not claimed read in full. This is a named reader, not Bederman’s own testimony or proof that she studied London in this way.

reading_limit: New identity is the Notre Dame historian and sole author of the selected writings. Both early articles and full monograph unread. Argument evidence is limited to the indexed primary passage and Harvey’s explicitly attributed discussion; direct scan access failed. The primary extract preserves differences among the historical actors. No claim of a uniform white masculinity or a direct intellectual influence on later scholars.

relations.relationship: Treats ideals of manhood as historical constructions whose forms and political uses change.
relations.evidence_note: Selected primary indexed passage, pp. 42–43, plus Anne-Marie Harvey’s substantive reading at printed pp. 42–43. The latter names Bederman’s distinction and extends it in her own study; her additions are not reassigned to Bederman.

relations.relationship: Investigates how claims about civilization could authorize white male power or be turned against it.
relations.evidence_note: Primary chapter-1 closing passage on four distinct cases, indexed printed pp. 42–43. The prose on historical actors is Bederman’s argument, not an endorsement of their racial categories. No claim that the entire book or its cited archival evidence was independently read.
